recent_posts.title: Why Be a Member of an Open Source Foundation?
recent_posts.summary: Open source foundations like the CD Foundation maintain critical infrastructure projects such as Jenkins, Spinnaker, and Tekton that thousands of companies rely on daily. Despite widespread usage, most organizations don't financially support these foundations. The CD Foundation is calling for companies to become members and contribute to the sustainability and security of the open source tools they depend on, with membership fees starting as low as $2,500 for existing Linux Foundation members.

recent_posts.title: The Ingredients of the Cake: Recipes for Sustainable AI Delivery
recent_posts.summary: Using cake-baking as an extended metaphor, this piece breaks down the essential infrastructure components needed for sustainable AI delivery. Each ingredient represents a critical system element: CI/CD pipelines (flour), observability (eggs), governance (baking powder/salt), provenance (receipts), delegation logic (chefs), infrastructure (ovens), compute power (electricity), cooling (water), backup power (natural gas), ethics (fair-trade ingredients), data/vectors (flavorings), and AI agents (frosting). Real-world failures from Zillow, Knight Capital, Cambridge Analytica, SolarWinds, Uber, and others illustrate the consequences of missing each ingredient, along with specific tools and fixes for each component. The core argument: AI systems require disciplined engineering practices and cannot rely on experimentation alone.

recent_posts.title: Application Guide - CD Foundation
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide for open source projects applying to become Google Summer of Code (GSoC) mentor organizations, based on Jenkins' 90% acceptance rate over 10 years. Covers the complete timeline from October through program completion, including forming admin teams, recruiting mentors, creating project ideas, submitting applications, and managing accepted contributors through coding periods and evaluations.

recent_posts.title: Engineering Trust in AI-Native CI/CD: A Three‑Panel Deep Dive with CDF Ambassadors
recent_posts.summary: Three panel discussions from the Continuous Delivery Foundation explored how AI, LLMs, and automation are transforming CI/CD pipelines. Key topics included AI-native CI/CD design patterns, using AI agents to reduce pipeline complexity through automated failure diagnosis and support, and implementing observability for AI-driven systems. Panelists emphasized starting with small experiments, maintaining human oversight, ensuring data quality, and building on strong foundational practices rather than replacing existing systems entirely.

recent_posts.title: CD Foundation seeks Hacktoberfest contributors for cybersecurity guide
recent_posts.summary: The CD Foundation invites developers to contribute to their CI/CD Cybersecurity Guide during Hacktoberfest 2025. Contributors can earn digital badges by fact-checking, reviewing, and adding open-source security tools that comply with NIST's Secure Software Development Framework. The initiative welcomes first-time contributors and provides labeled GitHub issues, community support through Slack, and guidance from active maintainers.

recent_posts.title: The Agentic Layer: Why the Middle of the Cake Matters in AI-Driven Delivery – CD Foundation
recent_posts.summary: AI systems require robust infrastructure foundations to succeed at scale. While organizations chase AI capabilities, they often neglect the critical middle layer of CI/CD pipelines, observability, governance, and trust mechanisms. The article uses a cake metaphor where AI is the sugar (frosting) but CI/CD infrastructure is the sponge that provides structural integrity. Real-world examples like Air Canada's chatbot failure demonstrate the risks of deploying AI without proper delivery discipline, while Capital One's MLOps success shows the benefits of treating AI as part of established delivery pipelines. The emerging "Agentic Layer" concept addresses how AI agents interact with infrastructure while maintaining pipeline discipline and governance.

recent_posts.title: August 28 - CD Foundation
recent_posts.summary: A workshop covering how to apply DevOps and CI/CD practices to Apache Spark applications running on containerized platforms. The session demonstrates packaging Spark jobs as immutable artifacts, implementing automated quality gates including code and data tests, and promoting jobs through environments using pipeline-as-code. Key topics include the complete flow from commit to deployment, production considerations for platform teams including multi-tenant quotas and security, and practical templates for implementation.

recent_posts.title: How to Shift from Fixed to On-Demand Release Cadence
recent_posts.summary: Release on Demand (RoD) shifts software delivery from fixed schedules to readiness-based releases, allowing teams to deploy when code is tested and valuable rather than following calendar dates. The approach requires strong team culture with ownership mindset, comprehensive automation including CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code, and built-in governance through automated change management. A data platform team case study demonstrates successful transition from fortnightly to daily releases using Azure DevOps and ServiceNow integration, resulting in reduced risk and faster debugging through smaller, focused deployments.

recent_posts.title: cdcon 2025 Wrap Up
recent_posts.summary: cdCon 2025, the sixth annual continuous delivery conference, took place in Denver with 168 registered attendees. The event featured 27 sessions over three days, focusing on supply chain security, AI/MLOps impact on continuous delivery, developer experience, and observability. Co-located with Open Source Summit North America, the conference celebrated both experienced practitioners and newcomers in the CD community.

recent_posts.title: Tekton Pipelines Reaches 1.0: Stability Today, Innovation Tomorrow
recent_posts.summary: Tekton Pipelines has officially released version 1.0.0, marking a significant milestone for the cloud-native CI/CD platform. The release brings StepAction to General Availability, enhances the Git resolver, introduces HTTP resolver capabilities, and removes the deprecated ClusterTask resource. While the v1 API has been stable for over two years, this release solidifies the foundation for future development. The project is also transitioning to the CNCF for better community support and long-term sustainability, with future plans focusing on stability, performance improvements, and better observability features.

top_posts.title: How to Ace the (CGOA) Certified GitOps Associate Exam
top_posts.summary: The Certified GitOps Associate (CGOA) exam is an entry-level certification focusing on open GitOps standards and vendor-neutral concepts. The 90-minute, multiple-choice exam covers GitOps terminology, principles, related practices, patterns, and tooling. Preparation involves studying documentation, using tools like FluxCD and ArgoCD, and utilizing training materials from the Linux Foundation. On exam day, ensure a clean workspace and follow proctoring guidelines. Passing requires a score above 75%, and results are received within 24 hours.
